messages:
lina (Partner Eng): @here BlueArc's SI team ran into a blocker during MediScale staging push — init container keeps crashing on our private image. Can we do a quick arch triage?

jake (Solutions): sending logs would help. what error are you seeing?

lina (Partner Eng): main error from the pod:

```
Init container: entrypoint.sh failed (exit 1)
Error: failed to mount /var/run/kv: permission denied
Events:
  Warning  FailedMount  10s  kubelet  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kv-socket": hostPath type check failed: /var/run/kv is not a socket
```

lina (Partner Eng): BlueArc says this worked in their internal QA cluster. MediScale is on a hardened RHEL AMI with custom container runtime.

ada (ML Eng): Could be SELinux or hostPath semantics. If the init expects a unix socket but AMI has a directory it will fail. Check `ls -la /var/run/kv` on the node.

mike (Infra): oncall-bot, can we get node-level access? I'll try `ssh` into the failing node.

oncall-bot: Escalation created: INC-2029. Priority: P2. Pager duty: infra-oncall.

jake (Solutions): @nora can you confirm BlueArc's image entrypoint actually creates the socket before the init runs? Maybe ordering issue with systemd unit that BlueArc relies on.

nora (SI PM): pinged BlueArc eng now. They say the init expects a mounted volume from the marketplace image sidecar that our private deploy omits. They pushed a quick patch last night — might be a version skew.

lina (Partner Eng): Ok — two action items: 1) Mike to validate node path & SELinux. 2) BlueArc to confirm image variant (sha) we pulled. If mismatch we should fallback to last-known-good image via routing policy.

mike (Infra): I ran `ls` and `getenforce` on node: `/var/run/kv` is a directory and SELinux Enforcing. `ausearch` shows AVC denial for container_t trying to create a socket there.

ada (ML Eng): TL;DR: SELinux + hostPath dir = permissions block. Workarounds: run init as privileged (no), change mount type to socket (preferred), or SELinux policy delta. For fastest unblock, BlueArc can change init to create socket under /tmp then move (if permitted).

jake (Solutions): We should also open a short arch review with MediScale to confirm security posture — they intentionally lock down SELinux. Propose 30-min call in 30m to agree remediation and rollback.

nora (SI PM): Scheduled: https://cal.com/redwood/30?ts=2498767800 — added BlueArc eng, MediScale platform, infra-oncall, and partner eng.

lina (Partner Eng): I'll drop the runbook steps into this thread for the call. If we need to rollback, we'll route traffic to `bluearc:v1.4.2` (sha: sha256:abc123) which we validated yesterday.

mike (Infra): Will attach node debug tarball to INC-2029.

jake (Solutions): Also note: if we end up changing the private deployment profile, we must update the marketplace image signing checklist and onboarding doc (docs/marketplace/onboarding.md) — flagging @docs.

lina (Partner Eng): thanks team. For now: triage call in 30m, BlueArc to verify image sha + push a socket-aware init, Mike to validate SELinux findings and test a mount tweak on a non-prod node. I'll update the incident and post a short postmortem template after resolution. :rotating_light:
